link.note: Andreas Grub's son Frederick is confirmed (1783 confirmation, 1791 will, mother's 1810 will); his identity with the Luzerne Frederick Croup who married Mary Young (Harvey Book) is probable-to-confirmed; WikiTree's child table gives Frederick's wife as Maria Jung and death 1841.

summary: John's 5th-great-grandfather; son of a Palatine immigrant at Easton who moved about 1800 to the Susquehanna river flats at Hunlock's Creek/Nanticoke and owned 'Stewart's Flats' in Plymouth.
bio: Frederick Grub was confirmed at St. John's Lutheran, Easton, in 1783 aged 15 as a son of Andreas Grub, placing his birth about 1767-68 (tree: no birth date, d. 1841). He and his mother were executors of his father's 1791 will; he was in Forks Twp in the 1800 census and co-executor with his mother in an Aug 1800 Northampton deed, and inherited jointly with his brother John. His mother's 1810 will names 'her son Frederick Krub'. About 1799-1800 he moved to Luzerne County: Bradsby says that 'soon after' about 1790 'Fredrick Croop settled near the river and opened the I. Davenport farm' at the mouth of Hunlock's Creek, while John Croop and the Sorbers settled further up the creek, and the 'Sorbers and Croops were mill men and built the sawmills'. The Forks census and deed suggest the move was really c.1800; daughter Susan was born at Nanticoke (WikiTree: Shickshinny) in May 1800. A captive's 1833 narrative says Indians killed Asa Upson on 28 Mar 1780 at 'Stewart's Flats, now owned by Frederick Croup, in Plymouth', and the 'Dutch Fishery' shad haul below Nanticoke used 'the upper end of the Croup farm' as its landing (confirmed that a Frederick Croup owned it by 1833; probable it is this man). His brother Philip's 1812 will named 'my dear brother Frederick Grupe' co-executor (Luzerne Will Book A p.128). Judge Thomas Cooper (1806-1811) jailed 'a gentleman named Croup' and Kingston constable Stephen Hollister for whispering in court - one of the charges that led to Cooper's removal in 1811; which Croup is unknown (speculative). The Croop mills and later Croop's Glen amusement park descend from his nephew John Croop's line, not his; Frederick was a farmer and landowner near the river. He married Mary Young ('Frederick and Mary (Young) Croup', Harvey Book p.354). Known children: Susan (1800-1863, m. Philip Shupp Jr.) and Elizabeth (1802-1895, m. James Pringle). An unverified Ancestry list (WikiTree Grub-81) gives Sarah, Elizabeth, Mary, Margaret, Catherine, William, Peter and Ann (omitting Susan); FamilySearch gives Susan, John, Peter, Mary, Margaret, Catherine, Ann and William. Both he and Mary are said to have died in 1841; no record of the deaths was found online.
funFacts: His farm at Stewart's Flats was the site of the 1780 killing of Asa Upson in an Indian raid.
His farm was the landing for the 'Dutch Fishery' shad haul at the Nanticoke narrows.
